draft.shortGloss: to look at; to check; to look after
draft.emotion: attentive and focused, turning attention toward something specific
notes: Also very common in the shorter form κοιτάω (or κοιτώ). Aorist: κοίταξα; imperative: κοίτα! ('look!').
Unlike English 'watch', watching TV or a film in Greek uses βλέπω (βλέπω τηλεόραση), while κοιτάζω means directing your eyes at something.

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something.

examples.text: Κοιτάζω τη θάλασσα από το παράθυρο.
examples.translation: I look at the sea from the window.
examples.emotion: calm and peaceful, enjoying the view outside

senses.definition: To examine or check something to get information or see its condition.

examples.text: Πρέπει να κοιτάξω την ώρα πριν φύγω.
examples.translation: I need to check the time before I leave.

senses.definition: To take care of someone or attend to a matter.

examples.text: Η γιαγιά κοιτάζει τα παιδιά το απόγευμα.
examples.translation: Grandma looks after the children in the afternoon.

draftBefore.shortGloss: to look at; to watch; to check
draftBefore.emotion: attentive and focused, turning attention toward something specific
notes: Koitazo is the standard, everyday verb for looking at or watching something, much more common than the formal vlepo in many active contexts.
Do not confuse it with koimamai, which sounds somewhat similar at the start but means to sleep.

senses.definition: To turn your eyes towards something to see it.

examples.text: Κοιτάζω τη θάλασσα από το παράθυρο.
examples.translation: I look at the sea from the window.
examples.emotion: calm and peaceful, enjoying the view outside

senses.definition: To watch something, such as a screen, a show, or an event.

examples.text: Το βράδυ κοιτάζω τηλεόραση με την οικογένειά μου.
examples.translation: In the evening I watch television with my family.
examples.emotion: relaxed and comfortable at the end of the day

senses.definition: To check or inspect something to see its condition.

examples.text: Πρέπει να κοιτάζω την ώρα πριν φύγω.
examples.translation: I need to check the time before I leave.
examples.emotion: slightly hurried, mindful of the schedule

faults.quote: much more common than the formal vlepo in many active contexts.
faults.why: False claim: βλέπω is completely neutral, everyday, and is the normal verb for watching TV.

faults.quote: Το βράδυ κοιτάζω τηλεόραση με την οικογένειά μου.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation in Greek; watching TV is 'βλέπω τηλεόραση', not 'κοιτάζω τηλεόραση'.

faults.quote: Πρέπει να κοιτάζω την ώρα πριν φύγω.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: before a single future event ('πριν φύγω'), perfective 'να κοιτάξω' is required.
